scope.runtime_reason: Direct producer, registration, outer-ProcessQueue, record-walker, second-processor, and ownership bytes already separate immediate send from deferred post, distinguish 0x14 registration records from 0x18 queue records, and establish that 0x008841f0 is cleanup/storage walking rather than dispatch. Runtime would refine reentrancy, cross-thread timing, and exact frame placement, but would not decide the minimum transport abstraction.

classification_taxonomy.use: Every event-family matrix row and every adversarial-step classification uses exactly one of these four values. Resolution status uses the campaign taxonomy.

hypotheses.name: universal_event_abi
hypotheses.claim: App messages, UTFWin messages, animation records, deferred events, communication events, and anonymous space records share one universal payload/event ABI.
hypotheses.prediction: A shared semantic field-wise ABI prefix or base subobject, universal queue carrier, universal callback shape, and shared ownership/order rules should exist across families.
evidence_for: Several event-like records expose a 32-bit ID and pointer or scalar fields.
Some domain messages can be transported by the App cMessageManager.
evidence_against: The tested field prefixes are not one semantic ABI: StandardMessage begins MultithreadObject vtable, refcount, five parameters; UTFWin::Message begins IWindow source, field_04, eventType; AnimationMessage begins uint32 messageID, char* name, creature pointer; cCommEvent begins ISimulatorSerializable vtable, IVirtual vtable, refcount, event type; the anonymous 0x6c/0x60 space records begin with opaque discriminators and timestamp-like words.
Incidental 32-bit pointer or scalar first words do not establish a shared base subobject: pointer roles and refcount offsets differ, and no tested family begins with the same semantic sequence.
Registration Entry is 0x14 bytes, while deferred queue records copied by producers and the record walker are 0x18 bytes with a distinct six-dword transport layout.

Callback contracts differ: bool HandleMessage(uint32,void*), void MessageHandler_t(uint32,void*,void*), UTFWin filter/priority/proc callbacks, runtime communication-domain cCommEvent with a persistence interface, and value-owned deferred records.

cCommEvent is a runtime communication-domain object that crosses into persistence through ISimulatorSerializable; it is not a persistence-only record, and no direct App queue edge is shown. The anonymous space pair belongs to a separate space state-handler SCC.

hypotheses.name: single_app_record_abi
hypotheses.claim: Inside App messaging, registration metadata and deferred delivery use one universal event record.
hypotheses.prediction: The same object should be inserted into the listener map, carried in the queue, and passed to callbacks without a layout or ownership transition.
evidence_for: Both registration and delivery are selected by the same 32-bit message ID and eventually reach the same listener/callback vocabulary.
evidence_against: The 0x14 Entry is copied into 0x1c allocated linked-list nodes as registration metadata.

The 0x18 queue record is built by FUN_00885890/FUN_00885930, copied by the 0x00884550 record walker, and consumed by the 0x00884700 second processor; its fields are message ID, payload, optional listener, integer ordering key, optional handler, and context.
Registration can fan out by priority; a deferred post targets one snapshot listener or one callback/context pair and the processor has a distinct three-way dispatch branch.

hypotheses.name: send_post_aliases
hypotheses.claim: MessageSend, MessagePost, and MessagePostFunction are naming variants over one timing and ownership contract.
hypotheses.prediction: Each surface should enqueue the same record, retain/release the same objects, and dispatch at the same phase.
evidence_for: All three are adjacent IMessageManager methods and share message ID and payload concepts.
evidence_against: The MessageSend body around 0x008854a0 locks, looks up the listener map/list, and invokes matching entries before returning; it does not call the queue insertion helper 0x00885710.
MessagePost around 0x00885980 and MessagePostFunction at 0x00885930 both build a 0x18 record and call 0x00885710.

MessagePost/Function optionally retain the payload and target before insertion and release them after callback; MessageSend accepts an unmanaged payload/listener and shows no queue ownership transfer.
The listener callback returns bool, but the deferred processor ignores it and dispatches every queued record; MessageHandler_t is void.

hypotheses.name: shared_transport_implies_shared_family
hypotheses.claim: If a record uses the App transport, it belongs to the same ABI/ownership/order family as StandardMessage.
hypotheses.prediction: All App-transported records could be represented as StandardMessage-derived 0x40 values and inherit the same callback and ordering rules.
evidence_for: The App transport passes a generic void* and therefore can carry many domain payloads.
evidence_against: The transport deliberately separates registration Entry, queue record, and payload object; payload interpretation is listener-specific.
Editors::cEditorAnimEvent MessageSend/MessagePost at 0x0059d8b0/0x0059d840 are not recovered as IMessageManager calls; they pack a 0x30 editor record and call different IAppSystem virtual slots.
UTFWin, tDeferredEvent, cCommEvent, Cell interaction records, and anonymous space records have separate owners and dispatch paths.

hypotheses.name: common_bus_global_order
hypotheses.claim: One common event ABI provides a total ordering guarantee across all event families.
hypotheses.prediction: A send or post in one family would establish observable order relative to UI, animation, deferred, communication, and space records.
evidence_against: Only the App bus has a recovered listener registry and queue processor.
UTFWin priority/filter order, tDeferredEvent scheduler order, cCommEvent presentation order, animation delivery, and space-record SCC order remain separate contracts.
A shared message ID namespace, where present, does not imply a shared clock, queue, or release boundary.

hypotheses.name: bounded_app_transport_abstraction
hypotheses.claim: OpenSpore needs an immediate broadcast/target dispatch surface, a deferred targeted surface, typed registration metadata, and family-specific payload views, but no universal payload record.
hypotheses.prediction: This minimum separates the architecture-deciding facts from unresolved binary quirks while preserving family ownership and avoiding false cross-family order.
evidence_for: Immediate and deferred producers/processors have different call paths and record lifetimes.
Registration and queue records have different layouts and responsibilities.
The event-family corpus supplies multiple independent owner/layout boundaries.
evidence_against: The unresolved +0x14 function target in the structurally identified concrete vtable, signed queue-key semantics, thread affinity, and queued cancellation remain open; these do not invalidate the minimum semantic split.

adversarial_steps.name: universal_record_test
adversarial_steps.prediction: If one universal ABI exists, a shared semantic field-wise prefix/base subobject, callback target, owner, and order contract should converge.
evidence_for: All candidate families have event-like IDs and are sometimes described as messages.
evidence_against: At offset 0, StandardMessage stores a MultithreadObject vtable, UTFWin::Message stores an IWindow source, AnimationMessage stores a uint32 message ID, cCommEvent stores an ISimulatorSerializable vtable, and each anonymous space record stores an opaque discriminator.

The next words are also semantically incompatible: StandardMessage refcount versus cCommEvent second vtable then refcount, UTFWin field_04/eventType, AnimationMessage name/creature pointers, and space mode/derived or timestamp-like words.
Therefore no tested family exposes a shared semantic field-wise ABI prefix or base subobject; the incidental common word width is not a shared type.
adversarial_steps.independence: The field-wise test uses independently queried live Ghidra structures/raw record writes, not the historical size-only comparison; equal use of the word message is not evidence.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Multiple historical reports repeat the family list, but those reports share the same SDK/type corpus and are counted once for independence.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Common event vocabulary survives, but no shared semantic ABI prefix/base subobject survives; the universal payload ABI is rejected independently of record size.

adversarial_steps.name: entry_queue_separator
adversarial_steps.prediction: Registration and delivery should share a carrier if they are one record ABI.
evidence_for: Both are keyed by message ID and refer to listener/callback metadata.
evidence_against: AddEntry at 0x00884c80 copies five Entry dwords into a 0x1c linked node and orders by Entry priority.
MessagePost/PostFunction build six dwords and 0x00885710 inserts them into 0x18 queue storage.

0x00884550 is the record walker: it copies six dwords and advances the 0x18-stride storage cursor. 0x00884700 is the second processor and dispatches through listener, handler/context, or owner fallback branches.
adversarial_steps.independence: Registration insertion, deferred insertion, dequeue, and dispatch are different function bodies. The producer/consumer field correspondence is reciprocal structural evidence, not two independent semantic discoveries.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Repeated 0x18 strides inside the same allocator helper are repetition within one implementation, not independent corroboration.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: After the cross-family semantic-prefix test fails, the smallest App-internal separator is the 0x14 registration Entry versus the 0x18 queue record. They are distinct transport-state records, not merely two sizes.

adversarial_steps.name: immediate_deferred_test
adversarial_steps.prediction: Aliases should share a call edge to the same queue insertion helper.
evidence_for: The methods are adjacent in the SDK interface and share ID/payload parameters.
evidence_against: The MessageSend body at the 0x008854a0 branch performs direct map/list lookup and callback invocation and lacks a 0x00885710 enqueue edge.
The 0x00885980 MessagePost body and 0x00885930 MessagePostFunction body both call 0x00885710.
Outer ProcessQueue at 0x00884100 calls the second processor at 0x00884700 through the +0x38 virtual slot; 0x008841f0 is not that dispatch entry.
adversarial_steps.independence: Direct producer control flow and an independent processor call path distinguish timing; SDK names alone do not.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The same immediate/deferred distinction is repeated in mode, editor, and event-map artifacts, but those narratives are not counted as independent binary proof.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: MessageSend is immediate; MessagePost and MessagePostFunction are deferred. Exact queue-key naming and reentrancy remain bounded limits.

adversarial_steps.name: subscriber_callback_abi_test
adversarial_steps.prediction: A universal callback ABI would use one target shape and one result convention.
evidence_for: IMessageListener and MessageHandler_t are both registered through the same Entry/list infrastructure.
evidence_against: IUnmanagedMessageListener::HandleMessage is bool(uint32,void*) at vtable +0x04.
IMessageListener adds AddRef +0x08 and Release +0x0c.
MessageHandler_t is void(uint32,void*,void*) and receives a context pointer.
FUN_00884700 branches among listener, handler/context, and an untargeted MessageSend fallback.
adversarial_steps.independence: SDK slot declarations, registration raw bytes, and deferred dispatch raw bytes are separate evidence classes.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Listener and handler entries share priority storage, but that shared storage is not proof of a shared invocation ABI.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Use a tagged target union conceptually: listener, callback/context, or broadcast. Do not erase the bool/void return distinction.

adversarial_steps.name: ownership_release_test
adversarial_steps.prediction: A universal queue record would have one ownership rule for payload and target.
evidence_for: All deferred records are copied through the same queue helper.
evidence_against: With the manager +0xc4 refcount option, post paths call payload vtable +0x04 AddRef and either listener vtable +0x08 AddRef or handler(1,0,context) before insertion.
After callback, the processor calls listener Release at +0x0c or handler(2,0,context), then payload Release at +0x08.
RemoveEntry separately releases a refcounted registration entry, and MessageSend is the unmanaged/borrowed surface.
When +0xc4 is false, the examined deferred path does not retain payload or target across enqueue.
adversarial_steps.independence: Pre-enqueue retention, post-callback release, and registration-removal release are separate control-flow sites.
adversarial_steps.repetition: MessagePost and PostFunction repeat the same refcount protocol; this is convergent transport behavior, not proof of cross-family ownership.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The App transport has an explicit retained-payload mode and a borrowed/no-retain mode. Other families retain independent ownership rules.

adversarial_steps.name: processor_consume_test
adversarial_steps.prediction: A bool HandleMessage result might consume/stop a message and explain multiple processor paths.
evidence_for: IUnmanagedMessageListener::HandleMessage returns bool in the SDK declaration.
evidence_against: FUN_00884700 stores no tested result from the +0x04 listener call; execution always reaches target release and the next dequeue condition.
MessageHandler_t returns void, so listener and callback targets cannot share consume semantics.
The queue record is removed by FUN_00884550 before callback invocation.
adversarial_steps.independence: The SDK return declaration and the processor control flow are independent; the processor wins for actual consume behavior.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Immediate and deferred paths both iterate entries/records rather than branching on a common consume bit.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The recovered App transport is broadcast-to-target, not first-handler-wins. Consume/cancellation must not be added to the minimum abstraction without new evidence.

adversarial_steps.name: priority_tie_order_test
adversarial_steps.prediction: If registration and queue records are universal, one priority rule should explain both.
evidence_for: Both Entry and queue record contain a 32-bit integer that can be called priority.
evidence_against: AddEntry compares linked-node priority and inserts a new entry before the first existing priority less than or equal to it, giving descending immediate registration order and newest-first equal-priority ties.

Deferred insertion at 0x00885710 compares queue record +0x0c and uses ordered insertion around a left-end dequeue; ordinary positive equal keys remain after existing equals. The signed-zero boundary and semantic name are not fully recovered.
The two integers occur in different record roles and are not proven to share units or direction semantics.
adversarial_steps.independence: Registration ordering and deferred insertion are separate algorithms. Their similar field type is not independent proof of one priority concept.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Several queued producers repeat the same six-dword template; only the insertion and processor algorithms are counted as independent mechanisms.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Freeze immediate registration order (descending, equal-newest-first) and treat deferred +0x0c as an ordering key with bounded lower-first semantics; do not promise a shared priority abstraction across both records.

adversarial_steps.name: cancel_snapshot_drain_test
adversarial_steps.prediction: A universal event record should support one cancellation model from registration through queued delivery.
evidence_for: Registration removal and deferred delivery are both owned by cMessageManager.
evidence_against: RemoveEntry at 0x008845d0 searches the message-ID registration list and optionally priority, then unlinks the registration node; no queued-record removal is present in the examined vtable/helpers.

The second processor at 0x00884700 snapshots the initial record count and processes at least that many; when manager +0xc3 is set it continues until the queue empties, allowing callback-produced posts to extend the drain. 0x00884100 is the outer bounded ProcessQueue entry, while 0x008841f0 is only a cleanup/storage walker.
A deferred record stores target pointers/snapshots rather than an Entry pointer, so unregistering an Entry is not shown to cancel an already queued delivery.
adversarial_steps.independence: Registry removal, queue dequeue, and processor loop bounds are separate bodies.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The historical claim that cancellation is unresolved is repeated across reports; current direct control flow narrows but does not globally prove the absence of an undiscovered cancel path.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Registration removal and queued delivery are separate lifecycles. Do not promise queued cancellation; expose bounded snapshot/drain processing.

adversarial_steps.name: family_smallest_separator_test
adversarial_steps.prediction: The architecture changes materially depending on whether one universal event ABI or a family-separated transport is used.
evidence_for: The App bus has a reusable ID/target/queue abstraction independent of payload schema.
The field-wise test finds no shared semantic ABI prefix or base subobject across the tested families.

UTFWin, editor animation, deferred city events, cCommEvent runtime/persistence domain state, Cell interactions, and anonymous space records have separate owners, layouts, and callback/dispatch contracts.
evidence_against: Using StandardMessage or cCommEvent as the universal envelope would erase UI filtering, animation targets, scheduler value ownership, serialization, and space-domain allocation.
Assuming cross-family total order would require an owner and clock that the corpus does not provide.
adversarial_steps.independence: The queue/transport evidence is independent of family-specific layouts and owners; the final synthesis is performed by the primary investigator.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Family separation appears in several reports, but shared historical source ancestry means it is counted as convergent static support rather than independent runtime proof.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Universal ABI rejected. Minimum architecture: immediate App dispatch + deferred App post + typed registration/queue state + family-specific payload views; no cross-family total order.

address_adjudication.result: The follow-up boundary/xref pass separates the outer ProcessQueue entry, queue record walker, cleanup/storage walker, and second processor. Historical SDK/Ghidra labels at interior or cleanup addresses are retained only as provenance and are not function roles.

items.result: The raw 0x008839a0 body constructs a 0x14 Entry with priority/refcount/handler/object cleared and calls IMessageManager+0x44. 0x00883a90 is in adjacent removal/helper code.
The raw 0x008839e0 body sets Entry.mbRefCounted, optionally calls listener AddRef, and calls AddEntry. 0x00883ad0 is not the AddListener body entry.
The raw 0x00883a30 body builds listener-as-function, priority, refcount flag, handler, and object before optional retain and AddEntry. 0x00883b20 is not the AddHandler body entry.

Walks 0x18-stride/0xc0-block queue storage and releases storage/object pointers through FUN_00f47380 during teardown. It does not copy the six record words or dispatch listener/handler/owner branches.
Checks manager+0xc2, computes queue-count-like state, applies a stack-supplied loop/timing bound, and invokes [vtable+0x38], reaching the second processor at 0x00884700.
Copies the six queue-record words, advances by 0x18, and transitions to the next 0xc0 usable block; it is distinct from both processors.

Calls 0x00884550, updates counters, dispatches listener/handler-context/owner-fallback records, conditionally releases, and implements the bounded-pass/drain loop. 0x00847f0 is an interior historical address.

items.concrete_body_anchor: body around 0x008853e7; immediate listener/handler branch at 0x008854a0
items.result: 0x008854a0 is an interior dispatch branch, not a function entry.
0x00885980 is the enqueue tail inside the deferred listener-target body.
0x00885a20 lies in a 0x18-record comparator/helper, not the callback-post body. The callback/context producer is 0x00885930.

ownership_evidence: Teardown body 0x00884fb0 writes 0x01427920 to object+0x00 before the cleanup path.
Table word +0x00 points to 0x00885390, whose body calls 0x00884fb0, matching a destructor slot.
The table contains 19 consecutive 4-byte words from 0x01427920 through 0x01427968; strings begin around 0x0142796c.
vtable_ownership.reconciled_role: 0x008841f0 is absent from the table; its teardown caller 0x00884fb0 independently explains its cleanup/storage-walker body. 0x00884550 is an internal record walker called by 0x00884700, not a vtable processor entry.
vtable_ownership.unresolved: The +0x14 word is 0x008853b0, for which current Ghidra reports no function. It is not repaired or named from this table.

registration_entry.role: Persistent per-message-ID subscription metadata; copied into 0x1c linked-list nodes.

deferred_queue_record.role: One deferred delivery snapshot; not a registration Entry and not a domain payload. 0x00884550 walks/copies records, while 0x00884700 dispatches them.
deferred_queue_record.block_surface: 0x18 record stride in 0xc0-byte usable blocks; the exact names/ownership of manager range/cursor fields remain unresolved.

immediate.target: optional unmanaged listener target; otherwise matching registered entries
immediate.order: registration priority descending; equal-priority newest entry first
immediate.consume: HandleMessage bool is not used to stop traversal
immediate.ownership: unmanaged/borrowed payload surface; no deferred queue retention established

deferred.timing: insert through 0x00885710 and dispatch only in a later processor pass
deferred.target: one listener snapshot or one handler/context pair
deferred.order: queue +0x0c ordering key; ordinary positive lower-first, equal existing-before-new; exact signed-zero semantics deferred
deferred.consume: listener bool ignored; handler is void
deferred.ownership: with manager +0xc4, payload and target are retained before enqueue and released after callback; without +0xc4, no cross-enqueue retain is established
deferred.processor: 0x00884550 is the record walker; 0x00884700 is the second processor and handles at least the initial snapshot, with +0xc3 enabling drain-until-empty; outer ProcessQueue 0x00884100 applies enable/count/time-like bounds

removal.behavior: Finds the message-ID registration list, matches listener or handler and optional priority (-9999 wildcard), conditionally releases a refcounted registration, unlinks one node, and removes an empty list.
removal.queued_cancel: not exposed or observed in the examined queue records/helpers

rows.ownership: manager owns registry and queued snapshots; retained mode conditionally owns payload/target references
rows.order: immediate descending priority/newest-first ties; deferred ordering-key queue; snapshot or drain-until-empty

rows.abi: 0x40 bytes: refcount, five 8-byte parameter slots, ID, and trailing flags/fields
rows.ownership: domain/refcount object; App transport ownership is conditional and separate from the record's own meaning
rows.order: domain record order only when posted through the App queue; no standalone total order

rows.abi: 0x0c exported base plus type-specific payload at logical +0x0c; IWinProc has priority/filter/handle slots
rows.ownership: Window/widget/proc graph; no proven App queue ownership
rows.order: priority exists, but traversal, bubbling, tie order, and return consumption are unresolved

rows.abi: 0x18 AnimationMessage; 0x30 refcounted cEditorAnimEvent with editor model/event/scalars
rows.ownership: animation/editor subsystem; cEditorAnimWorld owns intrusive editor records; pName lifetime unresolved
rows.order: editor Send/Post differ by IAppSystem slots; final animation delivery order unresolved

rows.abi: 0x1c POD: GUID, unaligned u64 trigger time, two floats, two uints
rows.ownership: vector/container-owned value; no vtable or App queue release protocol
rows.order: trigger comparison is intended, but epoch, same-time order, duplicates, expiry, and callback owner are unresolved

rows.abi: mode-specific type word at +0x24 and domain payload; no StandardMessage derivation
rows.ownership: Cell pool/queue releases each record after dispatch
rows.order: queued interaction dispatch order/timer coupling is separate from App message order

rows.abi: 0xa0 ISimulatorSerializable/refcount object with political, city/civ, mission, timing/priority, and response-vector fields

shared_semantic_abi_prefix_test.hypothesis: The tested event families expose one shared semantic field-wise ABI prefix or base subobject.

tested_records.prefix: +0x00 MultithreadObject vtable; +0x04 int refcount; +0x08 MessageParameter[5]; +0x30 uint32 id
+0x00 IWindow* source; +0x04 field_04; +0x08 eventType; payload variants begin at logical +0x0c
+0x00 uint32 messageID; +0x04 char* pName; +0x08 AnimatedCreature* pCreature
+0x00 ISimulatorSerializable vtable; +0x04 IVirtual vtable; +0x08 int refcount; +0x0c cCommEventType
0x6c/0x60 raw records: +0x00 opaque discriminator; +0x04 zero or mode/derived scalar; +0x08 timestamp-like value

shared_semantic_abi_prefix_test.incidental_overlap: Several records contain a 32-bit pointer or scalar at offset zero, but the pointed-to roles, following fields, and refcount positions differ. A common word width is not a common ABI.
shared_semantic_abi_prefix_test.conclusion: The universal payload-family ABI is rejected by the semantic prefix/base-subobject test independently of record size. The App 0x18 queue record is generic transport state and does not supply a shared payload base.

universal_abi_test.smallest_separator: At the first two 32-bit words, StandardMessage has MultithreadObject vtable/refcount, cCommEvent has ISimulatorSerializable vtable/IVirtual vtable, UTFWin::Message has IWindow source/field_04, AnimationMessage has message ID/name pointer, and the anonymous records have discriminator/derived words. No common semantic base subobject starts there. Within the surviving App family, the next separator is the 0x14 registration Entry versus the 0x18 queue record and its three-way dispatch.
universal_abi_test.result: The universal payload/callback/ownership/order hypothesis fails on field semantics, not merely size. A narrower universal App transport SPI survives.
universal_abi_test.what_would_change_it: A direct field/body test showing a common semantic base subobject across families, a direct body showing the same 0x14 Entry enqueued and consumed without a 0x18 transport record, or a direct cross-family path proving shared callback/ownership/order semantics would reopen the hypothesis.

resolution.architecture_decision: Adopt a family-separated event architecture with one bounded App transport SPI. Do not implement a universal event payload or promise cross-family ordering.
what_is_resolved: No tested event family shares a semantic field-wise ABI prefix or base subobject; incidental pointer/scalar width overlap is not ABI evidence.
Registration Entry and deferred queue record are distinct 0x14 and 0x18 state records.
MessageSend is an immediate registry traversal; MessagePost and MessagePostFunction enqueue 0x18 delivery records.
Listener and handler/context targets have distinct callback and return ABIs.
Deferred callback bool results are ignored; the recovered App processor has no first-handler-wins consume rule.
Immediate registration order is descending priority with equal-priority newest-first insertion.
Outer ProcessQueue is 0x00884100, 0x00884550 is the record walker, 0x008841f0 is cleanup/storage walking, and 0x00884700 is the second processor.
The second processor covers an initial snapshot by default and supports a drain-until-empty option.
With +0xc4 refcounting, payload and target are retained before deferred enqueue and released after callback.
Universal event ABI is rejected; family-specific payload schemas remain required.
what_is_not_resolved: Exact operation/function boundary for the structurally identified concrete vtable's unresolved +0x14 word 0x008853b0.
Semantic name/units and full signed-zero behavior of deferred queue key +0x0c.
Exact outer ProcessQueue time/count parameter semantics.
Thread affinity, recursive callback behavior, and lock policy across all callers.
A positive runtime trace of send/post, callback, and release order.
Queued cancellation outside the examined vtable/helpers.
UTFWin order/bubbling, tDeferredEvent scheduler order, cCommEvent codec/presentation order, animation final delivery, and anonymous space-record ownership/order.

transport: MessageId: typed 32-bit/hash identifier, with payload meaning owned by a family schema.
PayloadView: non-owning read-only view for immediate delivery; no universal StandardMessage layout.
SharedPayload: explicit retained payload for deferred delivery.
SubscriptionTarget: tagged listener or callback/context target.
Registration: message ID plus target, registration priority, and retained-registration policy.
QueuedDelivery: message ID, shared payload, target snapshot, ordering key, and enqueue sequence.
operations: dispatchNow(id, payload_view, optional_target): synchronous registry traversal.
post(id, shared_payload, ordering_key, listener_target): deferred targeted listener delivery.
postFunction(id, shared_payload, ordering_key, callback, context): deferred callback/context delivery.
process(max_count_or_budget, drain_mode): dispatch at least the current snapshot; optionally drain newly posted work until empty.
ordering_guarantees: Immediate eligible registrations run synchronously before dispatchNow returns.
Immediate registration order is priority descending; equal-priority registrations are newest-first to match recovered insertion.
No callback return consumes or stops later App deliveries.
Deferred deliveries are ordered by an explicit ordering key; retain an enqueue sequence as a deterministic tie-breaker rather than relying on the unresolved signed-zero native edge.
A normal processing pass covers records present at pass start. Drain mode may include posts made by callbacks until the queue is empty.
No ordering guarantee crosses App, UTFWin, animation, deferred-city, communication, Cell-interaction, or anonymous-space families.
ownership_guarantees: Immediate payload views are borrowed and valid only for the callback duration unless the caller supplies a separate retained type.
Deferred payloads and targets remain alive until delivery completes or the queued delivery is explicitly abandoned by an architecture decision.
Registration removal affects future dispatch, not an already queued target snapshot.
Queued cancellation is not part of the minimum contract until native behavior is resolved.
minimum_openspore_event_abstraction.family_rule: StandardMessage, UTFWin::Message, AnimationMessage/cEditorAnimEvent, tDeferredEvent, cCommEvent, Cell interaction records, and anonymous space records remain separate payload/owner contracts even when they use the App transport.

exact_dependent_decisions.decision: Reject a universal event payload ABI because the tested families have no shared semantic field-wise prefix/base subobject; preserve family-specific payload schemas.
Model registration Entry and deferred queue delivery as separate records with distinct responsibilities.
Expose immediate dispatch separately from deferred post; do not alias MessageSend with Post surfaces.
Represent listener and callback/context as tagged targets; preserve bool listener versus void handler behavior.
Do not stop App delivery on callback return; a bool result is informational in the recovered transport.
Freeze immediate registration order as descending priority with equal-priority newest-first insertion.
Use an explicit deferred ordering key plus deterministic enqueue sequence; do not assume registration priority and queue key are the same contract.
Use 0x00884100 as the outer ProcessQueue entry and 0x00884700 as the second processor; provide snapshot processing and explicit drain mode, with callbacks extending only drain-mode work.
Use explicit borrowed versus retained ownership; do not expose releaseable deferred pointers without a retained owner.
Treat registration removal and queued cancellation as different operations; omit queued cancellation until directly evidenced.
Keep UTFWin, editor/animation, deferred-city, communication, Cell-interaction, and anonymous-space ordering outside the App ordering contract.

Treat 0x01427920 as the structurally identified cMessageManager concrete vtable; assign +0x34 to outer ProcessQueue 0x00884100 and +0x38 to second processor 0x00884700; keep 0x008841f0 as cleanup/storage walking and 0x00884550 as the record walker.

blockers.blocker: The structurally identified concrete vtable +0x14 at 0x01427934 contains 0x008853b0, for which current Ghidra reports no function; its operation remains unrepaired.
blockers.next_observation: Resolve the concrete +0x14 pointer from a runtime object or independently verified relocation/table context, then correlate one slot call with the immediate map/list body around 0x008854a0.

blockers.blocker: Deferred key +0x0c direction is supported for ordinary positive keys, but its semantic name, units, and signed-zero behavior are not exact.
blockers.next_observation: Enumerate representative callers with constants and record a static insertion/dequeue table for negative, zero, equal, and increasing keys.

blockers.blocker: RemoveEntry unregisters a target, but queued records retain target snapshots; no examined path cancels queued delivery.
blockers.next_observation: Post to a refcounted target, remove its registration before the 0x00884700 second processor, and record whether delivery/release still occurs.

blockers.blocker: Thread affinity, recursive posts during immediate/deferred callbacks, and the exact lock domain are not established.
blockers.next_observation: A narrow trace with manager address, thread ID, lock calls, callback entry/exit, enqueue, and dequeue timestamps.

blockers.blocker: The anonymous space pair and tDeferredEvent ordering remain independent family blockers and cannot be repaired through the App queue ABI.
blockers.next_observation: Recover one construction-to-dispatch-to-release path for each family and compare ownership/order without adapting either to StandardMessage.

supporting_evidence_streams.result: Separates immediate traversal from deferred insertion and distinguishes outer ProcessQueue 0x00884100, record walker 0x00884550, cleanup/storage walker 0x008841f0, and second processor 0x00884700; it also recovers the six-dword queue record, target branches, snapshot/drain bounds, and post-callback release order.
Recovers 0x14 registration metadata, linked insertion order, handler/listener target representation, and registration removal/release.
Confirms separate owners, layouts, and callback/persistence contracts; no universal family ABI or cross-family total order.

subagent_status: No subagent interface was exposed. Three supporter-equivalent evidence streams were collected in parallel through independent read-only Ghidra and historical-artifact queries; the primary investigator performed synthesis and did not treat stream labels as independent agents.

limitations: No Ghidra mutation, disassembly creation, type application, labeling, saving, or project change was performed; only read/decompile/memory/call-graph tools were used with explicit program SporeApp.exe.
No SPORE/ filesystem traversal and no spore.db access were performed.
No implementation was performed and neither report is implementation authorization.
The current Ghidra program has no MSVC RTTI; 0x01427920 ownership is structurally identified as the concrete cMessageManager vtable by object assignment, teardown, and slot shape, not by RTTI.
SDK names/layouts are community-header provenance; direct target bytes outrank them where they conflict.
The structurally identified concrete vtable's +0x14 word 0x008853b0 has no current Ghidra function; its operation is explicitly blocked rather than silently repaired.
Deferred +0x0c lower-first ordering is static for ordinary positive keys; exact semantic and signed edge behavior remains unresolved.
No runtime evidence is claimed. The static architecture boundary is resolved, but runtime timing, thread behavior, and frame placement are not.
